originalGroup.material:
A. Planning outdoors and using an index

An outdoor class event needs more than a hopeful look at the sky. A useful weather plan explains what will happen if the original arrangement cannot go ahead. Thinking about the alternative in advance makes the final decision easier to communicate.

Name the conditions that would change the plan. "Bad weather" may mean different things to different people. ____1____ The conditions should relate to the activity, with safety decisions left to the responsible adults.

Choose a decision time. Families may need to arrange transport, and helpers need to know where to take equipment. ____2____ If conditions change unexpectedly later, send an update rather than pretending the earlier message remains sufficient.

Check the alternative space as carefully as the first one. A room may exist without being large enough or available. ____3____ Moving an event is useful only if the new arrangement can actually work.

Give people one clear place to find the decision. Some may hear a rumour from a friend before reading the official message. ____4____ A consistent source reduces the number of conflicting versions in circulation.

Finally, distinguish cancellation from postponement. ____5____ If there is no new date yet, say so. People can accept uncertainty more easily when they know which part has been decided and which part still needs an answer.

B. Planning outdoors and using an index

Our teacher asked us to find information in a long book without reading every page. I turned ____1____ (immediate) to the contents page, but it listed only broad chapter headings. The particular tool I wanted did not have a chapter of its own.

A classmate showed me the index ____2____ the back. It listed names and subjects in alphabetical order, together with page numbers. I found several ____3____ (reference) to the tool instead of just one.

The first page explained its basic use. Another contained a photograph, while a third compared an older version with a newer one. The index had helped me find the relevant places, but I still needed ____4____ (read) them to answer the question.

One entry said "see also" and directed me to a related subject. By ____5____ (follow) that link, I discovered a different term for the same kind of tool. Searching only the word I already knew would have missed it.

The book ____6____ (publish) before a recent change to the equipment. Our teacher reminded us ____7____ an index could guide us through a book without making the book current. We noted its date beside our answer.

At the end of the task, I could explain the difference between a chapter list and an index. Neither was ____8____ (good) for every purpose. What mattered was choosing the route ____9____ fitted the question. I wrote the page numbers in ____10____ (I) notebook so that I could return to the evidence instead of relying on memory.

A diagram can make an explanation easier to follow, but it achieves clarity by selecting what to show. Reading one well means noticing its conventions as well as its shapes. The picture and its labels need to be interpreted together.
